seoTitle: How to Upgrade Your Hostinger Plan and Balance
metaDescription: See how to upgrade a Hostinger hosting plan in 2026, including moving to VPS or cloud hosting, and how unused subscription balance carries over.
intro: As a website grows, a basic hosting plan can start to feel limiting, and upgrading on Hostinger doesn't have to mean losing money you've already paid. The upgrade screen automatically works out what you're owed from your current plan and knocks it off the new one, so the number you actually pay is almost never the sticker price. This guide walks through that comparison screen exactly as it appears — current plan versus upgrade, taxes, balance, and the final amount due — plus the billing-period choice that changes it all again.

steps.heading: Open the upgrade comparison for your site
steps.body: From the Websites section of your Hostinger dashboard, find the upgrade option for the site whose plan you want to change. It opens a two-column comparison: your Current plan on the left, and the plan you're upgrading to on the right, with a dropdown at the top of the right column letting you pick exactly which tier to move to. Each column lists its own price, visit limits, storage, RAM, CPU cores, PHP workers, and database connections stacked directly against each other, so you can see precisely what more money buys before committing to anything.

image.caption: The upgrade comparison screen. Current plan sits beside the upgrade target, with resource limits lined up row by row and the checkout summary on the right.

steps.heading: Pick the new plan from the dropdown
steps.body: The "Choose hosting plan" dropdown at the top of the right-hand column is where the actual selection happens — in this walkthrough it's set to Cloud Professional Hosting, one tier above the existing Cloud Startup plan. Changing this dropdown live-updates every number below it: the price, the resource table, and the checkout summary on the right all recalculate immediately, which makes it easy to flip between tiers and compare the real monthly cost of each before settling on one.

image.caption: The plan dropdown set to Cloud Professional Hosting, with the resulting price, resource table, and checkout total updating on the right.

steps.heading: See how your existing balance is applied
steps.body: This is the part most people are actually looking for. The checkout panel on the right lists Taxes & Fees, a Total, and then a line labeled Hostinger balance shown as a negative amount — this is the unused, already-paid portion of your current subscription being credited straight toward the new plan. Below that sits an optional coupon code field, and finally Amount To Pay, which is the real number you'll be charged after the balance and any coupon are subtracted. In the example shown, a 12-month upgrade with a substantial existing balance brought the amount due down to under ₹200, a fraction of the plan's sticker price.

image.caption: Choose billing period expanded to show 48-month and 12-month options, sitting directly above the balance-adjusted Amount To Pay.

steps.heading: Compare billing periods before you confirm
steps.body: Above the checkout summary, a "Choose billing period" control lets you switch between terms — commonly 12 months or a longer 48-month commitment. Each option changes both the monthly rate and how your existing balance gets applied, since a longer term spreads the same balance credit across a bigger total. It's worth toggling between the available periods once before paying, because the cheaper-looking monthly rate on a longer plan doesn't always mean a lower amount due today — the balance adjustment can make either option come out ahead depending on how much credit you're carrying.

steps.heading: Confirm and verify the new plan is active
steps.body: Once the plan, billing period, and any coupon are set the way you want, choosing a payment method finalizes the upgrade. Hostinger's summary also shows the new expiration date and the rate the plan renews at afterward, so there's no guessing what happens once the current discounted or balance-adjusted period ends. After confirming, it's worth checking your site loads normally and that the new resource limits reflect in your dashboard — the upgrade is designed to apply without downtime, but a quick check costs nothing.

faq.question: Will I lose money if I upgrade my Hostinger plan?
faq.answer: No — the checkout screen shows a "Hostinger balance" line that credits the unused portion of your current subscription directly against the new plan's cost, rather than charging you from scratch.

faq.question: Can I upgrade from shared hosting to VPS or Cloud hosting?
faq.answer: Yes. The "Choose hosting plan" dropdown on the upgrade comparison screen lets you select higher shared tiers or move up to Cloud Professional and similar plans, with pricing and resources updating live as you switch.

faq.question: Does the billing period I choose affect what I pay today?
faq.answer: Yes — switching between the available billing periods (for example 12 months versus 48 months) changes both the monthly rate and how your existing balance is applied, so it's worth comparing both before confirming.

faq.question: Does upgrading cause downtime?
faq.answer: The process is designed to be smooth, though it's a good idea to verify your site is functioning normally right after the upgrade completes.

faq.question: Where do I see the exact amount I'll be charged?
faq.answer: The "Amount To Pay" line at the bottom of the checkout summary is the final number after taxes, your Hostinger balance credit, and any coupon code have all been applied.
